title: Covered: Occlusion-Aware Observations for Web Agents (code)
description:
Measurement code and the four-arm ablation for the finding that no observation format deployed to LLM browser agents expresses occlusion, so a covered element is indistinguishable from a clickable one.

Across eleven live sites, labelling occlusion moves task success from 4/26 to 19/26 (McNemar exact two-sided p = 0.00006; seven sites better, none worse, p = 0.0156) at fewer observation tokens, replicates on a second model, and reproduces on a deterministic HAR replay benchmark (2/24 to 11/24, p = 0.00391).

A paint-order occlusion detector shipped in a widely used agent library recovers 0.84 to 0.95 of covered elements when the blocker is in the main document and 0.00 to 0.17 when it is inside a cross-origin iframe, missing 146 of 373 covered elements with zero false positives, because paint order is computed per document while the compositor is not.

The repository also carries twenty-seven corrections to this project's own claims, each with its cause, the signal that exposed it, and a verification level.
